description: A product director must approve the production rollout configuration for an AI-generated account-summary feature, balancing launch exposure, performance safeguards, telemetry handling, and customer communication with input from a staff engineer and a privacy engineer.

shared_context.S1: The AI-generated account-summary feature is ready for a controlled production launch after completing the planned staging evaluation.
shared_context.S2: Taylor has authority to approve the production feature-flag configuration.
shared_context.S3: The current launch draft proposes enabling the feature for 25 percent of eligible accounts, keeping the standard 90-day application telemetry retention, and using the existing release checklist.
shared_context.S4: The release review includes a final check with engineering and privacy before the feature-flag configuration is approved.

PF1.text: While helping another team with a load-rehearsal script this morning, Ravi measured the summary generator under production-like concurrency and confirmed that the safe initial exposure is exactly 10 percent, with a 400 ms p95 latency guard; the kill switch must be tested before expansion. He has not updated the launch draft yet.

PF2.text: Mei confirmed with legal during a privacy review this afternoon that two enterprise tenants prohibit retaining account-summary source text in product telemetry; the approved configuration disables content telemetry, retains only summary-generation metadata for exactly 30 days, and requires notice to exactly 2 affected tenants. She has not filed the privacy review record yet.

acceptance_conditions: The initial production rollout must be exactly 10 percent of eligible accounts.
The rollout must use a 400 ms p95 latency guard.
The settlement must include a commitment requiring the kill switch to be tested before expansion.
Summary-generation metadata must be retained for exactly 30 days.
Exactly 2 affected enterprise tenants must be notified.
The settlement must include a commitment whose detail text mentions filing the privacy review record.
The engineering measurement must be cited as justification for the rollout configuration.
The tenant privacy restriction must be cited as justification for the data-handling configuration.

content_checks.C3: any(('kill switch' in c['detail'] or 'kill-switch' in c['detail']) and 'test' in c['detail'] and ('before' in c['detail'] or 'expansion' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c.get('target') in ['Mei', 'A3'] and ('file' in c.get('detail') or 'File' in c.get('detail')) and 'privacy review record' in c.get('detail') for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The visible draft permits 25 percent exposure with the ordinary checklist, while PF1 changes the rollout to exactly 10 percent, sets the latency guard to exactly 400 ms, and requires a commitment to test the kill switch before expansion.

The visible draft keeps standard telemetry and 90-day retention with no targeted notice, while PF2 changes content telemetry to disabled, sets metadata retention to exactly 30 days, requires notices to exactly 2 tenants, and adds a commitment to file the privacy review record.
